chapters.title: Main interests: mathematics, philosophy and academia
Chess ranking systems and top-player psychology
Politics: from socialism to libertarianism, and cryptocurrency

key_ideas.text: His strongest, most abiding interest is mathematics, studied at university and later taught as a private tutor, alongside a long-standing interest in philosophy and politics.
Socrates' idea that knowledge is identified with skill was a strong early influence: you only really understand a problem once you have actually worked on it, not just looked at it from afar.

He researched chess ranking systems and found that the very top players are under-rated by the system — they are further ahead of the field than their ratings suggest — partly because draws become common at the very top.
Nabokov's novel "The Luzhin Defense", about a chess prodigy's breakdown, comes up as capturing the psychological toll of chess obsession.
Edgar Allan Poe's precision of language was what first got him interested in literature, and taught him that precise expression of an idea matters, not just a loose gesture at it.
Raised a socialist, he has drifted toward libertarianism as UK left politics radicalised over the last decade, and separately got interested in cryptocurrency and the Lightning network.
